title: openai-compat: tool calling -> tool_choice semantics + schema mapping + tool message formatting
author: Priya Rao
release_notes: Added OpenAI-compatible tool_choice semantics and schema mapping glue. Minor API surface adjustments for tool message formatting; default behavior preserved but opt-ins available. See migration notes for clients using raw tool payloads.
description:
Motivation: The OpenAI compatibility layer must correctly implement 'tool_choice' semantics and support flexible schema mapping and consistent tool message formatting so downstream SDKs (Python/TS/Go) and hosted integrations can interoperate with existing OpenAI-style tool calling flows. This PR implements the server-side semantics for tool_choice, a schema-mapping layer between Redwood tool schemas and OpenAI-style JSON schemas, and normalizes tool -> assistant message formatting (tool invocation / tool result) during streaming and non-streaming responses.

Summary of changes: 1) Implemented tool_choice semantics in the compatibility layer so assistant responses that select between multiple candidate tools are emitted as an OpenAI-compatible  "tool_choice" object in the response surface. 2) Added a schema-mapping utility that converts Redwood internal tool param schemas (YAML/Protobuf-like definitions) into OpenAI-compatible JSON Schema fragments, with optional per-tool overrides. 3) Normalized tool-call message formatting: tool invocation appears as assistant message with role "tool" and structured content; tool results are normalized into a single-line JSON payload when streaming, preserving chunked frames. 4) Updated SDK response parsing hooks and added opt-in compatibility flags: OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOL_MESSAGE_FORMAT=stable and OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOL_CHOICE=true for rollout. 5) Added a migration guide and unit/integration tests that exercise streaming path, tool_choice flows, and schema edge-cases.

Technical details and rationale: - tool_choice: Previously we emitted a custom Redwood event for selecting a tool; OpenAI compatibility requires a richer payload (tool name, reasons, and optional arguments). We now surface a consistent "tool_choice" envelope inside the assistant message metadata and in the compatibility response object to enable downstream clients that expect the OpenAI shape. This is opt-in to avoid surprising older clients. - Schema mapping: Redwood's tool param models are more expressive (typed enums, nested structs). The mapping layer flattens certain constructs and emits JSON Schema with metadata fields (examples, required, enum) and emits a provenance header so clients can determine if a mapping was lossy. - Message formatting: Streaming stability required small adjustments to how we emit framing for tool results (we now ensure each stream chunk is valid UTF-8 and that the reconstructed payload parses to the same JSON Schema). This reduces flakiness observed in long-running streaming tool runs. - Backwards compatibility: Default behavior is unchanged. All OpenAI-compat features are toggled via compatibility flags at the request level and via account feature flags.

Testing and QA: - Unit tests for schema mapper (roundtrip for typical Redwood tools). - Integration tests exercising tool_choice selection during beam-search and sampling modes. - Streaming canary jobs: perf-canary job ran 24h against a synthetic workload to validate no regression in latency or chunk loss. - Manual validation: SDK parsers (python/typescript) were run against recorded sessions.

Rollout plan: Feature gated; start with internal rollout for Redwood-hosted integrations, then opt-in for a subset of customers using OPENAI_COMPAT tool flags, monitor error rate and parsing failures for 48h, then default-on if no regressions.

Migration notes: Clients that parse raw tool payloads should switch to the compatibility parsing helpers provided in SDKs. If you previously relied on Redwood's internal param shapes, switch to the mapped JSON Schema or request raw_schema option in the mapping helper.

Related: Linear ENG-2148, PM-439, Support ticket SUP-4312.

discussion:
Ethan Brooks (reviewer): Can we make tool_choice opt-in at the request level rather than account-level?
Priya Rao (author): Yes; implemented request-level flag OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOL_CHOICE and account-level fallback. Updated tests accordingly.
Liam Patel (reviewer): Schema mapper may lose enum descriptions when flattening nested enums; add provenance metadata so consumers can detect lossy mapping.
Priya Rao: Added a 'mapping_provenance' metadata field with 'lossy=true' when we drop fidelity and added unit tests.
Zoe Martinez (reviewer): Streaming chunks looked fine in unit tests but I saw one intermittent failure in perf-canary. Can you add extra guards for invalid UTF-8 frames?
Priya Rao: Added normalization step that replaces invalid byte sequences with Unicode replacement char during framing and added canary run results to the PR.
Ethan Brooks: Approved after fixes.
Zoe Martinez: Approved.
